strings.name: Wael Sawan
strings.summary: Trained in engineering and business administration, Wael Sawan joined Shell in 1997 and led its Qatar, deepwater, upstream and integrated gas businesses before becoming CEO in 2023. His tenure has emphasised investment returns and oil and gas, alongside closely watched changes to the energy transition strategy and emissions targets.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026, with recent activity supported by an official record of a 4 November meeting. Corporate strategies and emissions targets are plans; lower carbon intensity does not necessarily mean lower total emissions.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads Shell and participates in strategic choices across international energy operations, natural gas, electricity and emissions-reduction investment.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned an MEng from McGill University in 1997 and also holds an MBA from Harvard Business School.
strings.facts.f2.label: International background
strings.facts.f2.value: Born in Beirut in July 1974 and raised in Dubai; holds Lebanese and Canadian citizenship.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Management across business divisions
strings.highlights.h1.text: Rose from engineering to group leadership, with management experience in upstream oil and gas, deepwater production and integrated gas.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Changes to energy transition strategy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Under his leadership, Shell emphasised returns and gas growth while easing some carbon intensity targets. These are changes to strategy and targets, not emissions reductions already achieved.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Met Kuwait's Crown Prince
strings.timeline.t1.text: Kuwait's Crown Prince Diwan recorded a meeting at Bayan Palace to discuss economic cooperation. The talks do not establish that a specific deal was signed.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Company revised carbon intensity targets
strings.timeline.t2.text: The 2030 net carbon intensity reduction target against 2016 levels changed from 20% to 15–20%, and the target of a 45% reduction by 2035 was withdrawn.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became Shell CEO and joined its board
strings.timeline.t3.text: Succeeded Ben van Beurden. The appointment was announced in September 2022 and took effect on New Year's Day 2023.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Took charge of integrated gas and new energy businesses
strings.timeline.t4.text: Succeeded Maarten Wetselaar as head of Integrated Gas, Renewables and Energy Solutions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became head of Upstream
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Andy Brown and joined the group Executive Committee. The announcement had been made in January that year.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Moved to executive vice president for Deepwater
strings.timeline.t6.text: Left the Qatar leadership role to oversee deepwater operations in the Gulf of Mexico, Nigeria and Brazil.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Promoted to lead the Qatar business
strings.timeline.t7.text: After several years working in Qatar, became vice president and chairman of the local Shell companies.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed an engineering master's degree and joined Shell
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned an MEng from McGill University and joined Shell that year, working as an engineer with Petroleum Development Oman.
